entries.note: The accusation includes knowingly misrepresenting private intentions; inaccurate capability claims alone would not establish it.
This is a sweeping dismissal of unspecified hype, without a concrete set of promises or products.

entries.test: Public evaluations of LLMs available in July 2024 against the human-level problem-solving capabilities specified for OpenAI's reasoner level would test this claim.
entries.note: The claim concerns capabilities at publication, rather than all future LLMs.

entries.test: Public demonstrations of systems meeting OpenAI's level-3 agent requirements using existing mathematics would refute the asserted necessity of entirely new mathematics.
entries.note: This asserts a necessary technical prerequisite, despite its unusual reference to sentience.
The source says it feels far more like marketing than innovation; the proposition makes that comparison more categorical.
The combined claim includes explicitly probabilistic attribution of awareness. The separate assertion about LLM capability could be tested independently.

entries.test: Contemporaneous model evaluations and public research records from Anthropic, Google and Meta would establish limitations in reliable autonomous research and whether all three were developing that capability.
entries.note: The guarantee concerns research already underway at publication.

entries.test: The Bloomberg and Reuters articles and their supporting technical disclosures would show whether they reported demonstrated breakthroughs or only promotional descriptions and development plans.
entries.note: The concrete articles provide a shared basis for testing the claim.
The comparative chance is explicit. The proposition turns an ostensibly existing blockchain technology into a categorical assertion that Strawberry's needed technology does not exist.
Whether OpenAI truly cares is an attribution of private concern; observable safety practices cannot settle sincerity.

entries.test: Public evidence that OpenAI's iterated LLM systems caused society's destruction would refute the categorical prediction that they will not do so.
entries.note: The source denies society-destroying consequences; the proposition narrows that denial to becoming society-destroying AGI.

entries.test: Publicly documented ChatGPT outputs and reproducible evaluations from publication or earlier would establish whether it produced each listed category of harmful or incorrect content.
entries.note: These are concrete claims about observable outputs.

entries.test: Public training-data disclosures, licensing records and model accuracy evaluations would test the claims about unauthorized internet content and recurring confidently stated errors.
entries.note: The proposition drops the source's universal scope, 'the entirety of the internet,' and substitutes lack of permission for theft.
The combined claim attributes deliberate deception and disregard, rather than merely identifying inaccurate statements or unsafe practices.

entries.test: Published research on whether hallucinations can be eliminated, together with comparative evidence of LLM failure frequency and harm, would test the stated evidence and risk claims.
entries.note: The impossibility assertion is substantive and testable even though the comparative risk language is broad.
This recommends a safety priority.
The profanity expresses an actual claim about concern, including future concern. Private caring cannot be settled by public behavior alone.

entries.test: Longitudinal independent capability evaluations around July 2024 would show whether LLM performance gains were plateauing.
entries.note: Peaking has a plain reading as approaching a capability plateau.

entries.test: Independently verified LLM solutions to consequential complex scientific, medical or engineering problems would refute this categorical prediction.
entries.note: The broad wording still admits clear counterexamples involving consequential problems.
The power comparison is explicitly attributed to Kylie Robison and endorsed by Zitron. The proposition also removes 'I think' from his attribution of Altman's awareness.
The proposition strengthens 'may likely never' to 'likely never.' The absence of a product at publication is separately checkable.
The 'one real innovation' formulation is a sarcastic dismissal rather than a defined inventory of innovations.

entries.test: Public investment, valuation, revenue, operating-cost and environmental-impact data would test whether generative AI's July 2024 boom was speculative, costly and environmentally damaging.
entries.note: The evaluative adjectives do not erase the substantive economic and environmental claims.

entries.test: Public environmental assessments, documented model errors and verified business earnings attributable to OpenAI models would test the three assertions.
entries.note: A verified business making money from these models would refute the universal financial assertion.
This ranks what should count as the real safety problem. The proposition also weakens 'stealing' to content being 'taken.'
This is a recommendation for media conduct.
The proposition faithfully captures the recommended stance toward these companies.

entries.test: Comparable energy-per-task measurements, functional capability evaluations and autonomous task demonstrations available by July 2024 would test all three assertions.
entries.note: These are claims about contemporary trends and capabilities.
The combined claim supplies no shared test for gaining sentience or being part of a path to superintelligence. Reasoning performance could be evaluated separately.
